title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go + parity fixes + version bump v1.199.0
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Unified auth + retry behavior across Python/TS/Go SDKs; improved streaming ergonomics and parity fixes. Bumped SDK package versions to v1.199.0. Backwards compatible for most users; see notes for auth config changes.
description:
Motivation: We have drift across the three official SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) in how auth is composed, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics. This causes product support overhead (token loss in partial streams, inconsistent retry backoff, and fractured developer experience). This PR unifies the public ergonomics and internal wiring so feature parity is maintained and releases can be automated across SDKs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Standardizes auth configuration: single 'ClientConfig' / 'Config' surface with unified env var fallbacks and clearer precedence (explicit params > env > shared config file).
- Unifies retry policy defaults: exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency-aware retries for non-streaming calls, and a configurable RetryPolicy object exported in all three SDKs.
- Improves streaming ergonomics: stable reconnect hooks, resumed-kv-caching tokenization note for Python/TS, and clearer guarantees on partial-message delivery.
- Parity fixes: aligned method names, parameter order, and error classes across SDKs to reduce cognitive overhead for cross-platform teams.
- Version bumps: v1.199.0 for the three SDK packages with changelogs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2024)
- [x] Unit tests added for retry/backoff decisions
- [x] Integration tests for streaming reconnect behavior
- [x] Docs updates in SDK READMEs and quickstarts
- [x] Release notes drafted

Commits (summary):
- "unify: export unified Config/ClientConfig and env precedence"
- "retries: introduce RetryPolicy with exponential backoff and jitter"
- "streaming: add reconnect hooks and resume behavior for partial streams"
- "python: adjust streaming iterator API for parity with TS/Go"
- "go: export new RetryPolicy and map error types to common SDKError"
- "chore: bump versions to v1.199.0 and update CHANGELOGs"

Changed areas / files (high level):
- sdks/python/redwood
  - redwood/config.py (new unified config loader)
  - redwood/retries.py (RetryPolicy implementation + tests)
  - redwood/streaming.py (reconnect/resume logic, iterator ergonomics)
  - setup.cfg / pyproject.toml (version bump)
- sdks/typescript/packages/redwood-sdk
  - src/config.ts, src/retries.ts, src/streaming.ts (parity implementations + types)
  - package.json (version bump)
- sdks/go/redwood
  - config.go, retries.go, streaming.go (parity + exported interfaces)
- docs/quickstarts/sdks.md (updated examples showing unified auth)
- tests/integration/streaming_resume_test.py (new), tests/e2e/retries_policy_test.ts (new)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Priya: "Thanks Jordan -- this is a big win. A couple of questions: 1) do we preserve previous env var names for backwards compatibility? 2) How will this affect users who relied on implicit retry behavior in older SDK versions?"
- Jordan: "We preserve legacy env var names as fallbacks (see config loader) and added deprecation warnings. Retry defaults are tightened but we preserve opt-out by allowing a no-retry policy. Added a migration note in the changelog and quickstart."
- Liam: "I found a race in the TS streaming reconnect path where abort signals could be dropped. Suggest adding an explicit abort handshake."
- Jordan: "Addressed in commit 'streaming: add abort handshake and explicit token checkpoint'. Re-added tests to cover the handshake."
- Chen: "Go linter flagged an exported type name mismatch; please ensure exported docs update reflects the new names."
- Jordan: "Renamed Go types to SDKError/RetryPolicy as requested and updated generated docs."

CI status: initial pipeline failed on flaky streaming integration tests (flake related to local port binding). Re-ran CI after adding tighter test isolation; pipeline passed all checks (unit, lint, typecheck, integration).

Merging notes: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Priya, Liam, and Chen. Coordinated release cut: packages were published to PyPI/npm/goreleaser artifacts as v1.199.0 with staged rollout to avoid API key churn for enterprise customers.

User-facing migration notes:
- Auth: users can keep existing env vars; explicit config now recommended. See updated quickstart for examples.
- Retries: default is safer (fewer duplicate side-effects) but opt-out available.
- Streaming: reconnect behavior improves resilience; some advanced users may need to update custom stream parsing logic to handle resumed segments.

If there are follow-ups: track under ENG-2099 for any post-release fixes and ENG-2024 for longer term ergonomics improvements.
